newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to visit Mexico, Caribbean, South America.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to visit Mexico, Caribbean, South America.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will visit Mexico on April 11-12 and make a separate trip to Barbados, Costa Rica, Brazil and Argentina on May 6-13, the White House said on Wednesday.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton would meet Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo during his April trip and discuss economic issues associated with the implementation of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), as well as immigration, fighting drug trafficking and environmental protection.
He said Clinton considered Mexico a close neighbour and partner and the United States had "a very direct interest in the recovery of the Mexican economy."

In his State of the Union speech to Congress on Tuesday evening, Clinton hailed the success of his controversial economic rescue package for Mexico. The president noted that Mexico had repaid all the money it borrowed from Washington and U.S. exports to its southern neighbour were at an all-time high.
Clinton will receive Chilean President Eduardo Frei in Washington on Feb. 26 and NAFTA is expected to be on the agenda then as well.

Chile would like to join NAFTA, but would prefer first that the Clinton administration get "fast track" negotiating authority from Congress that would prevent lawmakers from holding up the trade agreement or subjecting it to endless amendments.
Clinton urged Congress on Tuesday to give him this authority to assist in negotiating new trade pacts.
